title: Blue/Green + Shadow Validation + Snapshot Rollback runbook for VPC data-plane upgrades
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Objective: Deliver a deterministic, zero-downtime upgrade flow for Private (VPC) data-plane/runtime that combines blue/green activation with shadow-traffic validation and a fast snapshot-based rollback path. The outcome is an automated Terraform-driven orchestration + operator actions + runbook that ops or SRE can execute end-to-end with safety gates and clear escalation paths.

Acceptance criteria:
- Automated preflight validations (infra, KV cache health, disk free, kernel/driver compatibility) run and block rollout on failures.
- New runtime nodes are brought up in green pool without affecting production traffic; shadow traffic mirrors 10-25% of live requests for correctness checks.
- KV cache warmup completed to pre-defined hit ratio threshold before traffic shift.
- Observability gates (p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, throughput, KV miss rate, memory pressure) are enforced by a policy engine; breach triggers automated rollback.
- Fast rollback implemented via incremental connection quiesce + snapshot restore of runtime state and model-variant fallback; rollback completes within SLO-defined window (target 3 minutes for majority of tenants).
- Terraform modules included for orchestration primitives and versioned in terraform-private-modules repo.

Design summary:
1) Preflight phase (Terraform + operator checks): validate network routes, IAM/KMS access, node image compat, GPU driver version, and run unit synthetic probes. This is implemented as a terraform null_resource hook that calls the upgrade-orchestrator service with --validate.
2) Green pool provisioning: spin up new nodes with runtime image tagged to release candidate. Nodes register but remain in isolated pool. KV cache sharding performed with a warmup controller that streams hot keys from a history sampler.
3) Shadow validation: mirror a configurable percentage of live traffic (default 10%). Mirror client runs in synchronous mode for correctness checks (response diffing, determinism flags) and asynchronous mode for performance tracing. Validation window is configurable (default 15 minutes).
4) Gating: policy engine evaluates metrics from the console and Alertmanager. Gates include rolling median latency delta < 10ms, p99 delta < 50ms, error rate delta < 0.1%, KV cache hit ratio >= 80% of baseline, and no OOM or cgroup throttling events. Gates are modular and surfaced in the console.
5) Activation or rollback: if gates pass, traffic is shifted in stages (25/50/100). If gates fail or critical incidents detected, orchestrator triggers the rollback path: connection drain to green pool, restore snapshot for in-flight state where possible, switch to fallback model variant, and deprovision faulty nodes. Rollback steps are idempotent and logged.

Implementation tasks (high-level):
- Terraform: add upgrade_orchestrator module with hooks for preflight and activation, and a variable-driven shadow percentage. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-private-modules/pulls/142)
- Orchestrator: new endpoints for validate, mirror-start, gate-evaluate, activate-stage, rollback-snapshot. Add circuit-breaker integration with Alertmanager.
- Runtime agent: expose health-tagged metrics (kv_hit_ratio, cache_warm_pct, prewarm_status) and safe snapshot checkpoint API.
- Console: rollout UI to show gate status, shadow diffs, and one-click rollback.
- Runbook: step-by-step playbook for manual intervention and postmortem templates.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: shadow traffic causes increased upstream load or noisy metrics. Mitigation: rate-limit shadow traffic, run first in async validation mode, and preflight canary on low-volume tenants.
- Risk: KV warmup takes longer than expected for cold tenants. Mitigation: advance warmup sampling, pre-seed large keys, and allow progressive traffic ramp tied to cache hit thresholds.
- Risk: snapshot restore may not reconcile some ephemeral state. Mitigation: add conservative fallback to model-variant downgrade that preserves correctness at cost of lower perf.

Operational runbook highlights:
- Pre-upgrade: run terraform plan, validate preflight output, take scheduled snapshot (s3://private-upgrades/snapshots/{{date}}).
- During upgrade: monitor rollout UI, confirm shadow validator diffs <= 0.5% semantically significant changes, watch latency and OOM alerts.
- On gate breach: run `orchestrator rollback --snapshot <id> --reason <gate>`; if rollback fails, escalate to on-call SRE (pager) and follow manual snapshot restore steps.
- Post-upgrade: run smoke tests, notify customer contacts, and schedule 24-hour watch.

Notes on Terraform/IaC: the new module aims to be minimal in workflow surface area: a single module call returns an orchestrator endpoint and exposes variables for image_tag, shadow_percent, gate_policy_id, and snapshot_retention_days. We included example usage in the module README.

2025-02-18 Liam Chen: Prototype of terraform module merged to feature branch; basic validate hook implemented. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-private-modules/pull/142
2025-02-22 Maya Patel (review): Requested clearer rollback SLAs and an explicit snapshot archival strategy. Added to runbook.
2025-02-28 Jesse Park: Staging run produced p99 spike when shadow_percent=25% due to backend throttling. Mitigated by capping shadow concurrency and switching to async diffs for first 10 minutes.
2025-03-03 Liam Chen: Added gate for KV cache warmup (threshold 80%); updated orchestrator to surface warmup_pct metric. Deploying to canary tenants this week.

2025-03-05 QA (Jasper O'Neil): Integration test passes for basic scenarios; observed intermittent 503s on large payloads during activation stage. Follow-up investigation: batching kernel selection behavior on runtime images.
